brief: The Mag 7 and Nasdaq trade near their highs, but internals are diverging. The Mag 7's payout ratio has collapsed to 28% as cash shifts from buybacks to AI capex, and Fidelity's Timmer notes the group's relative performance peaked when the buyback era ended and has since diverged from absolute price. Carlyle frames this as record accounting profits paired with falling free cash flow. Credit is starting to question it: Apollo says hyperscaler CDS spreads have decoupled sharply higher from bank spreads even as equities keep celebrating the spending, and while 69% of S&P 500 firms report a live AI deployment, only 2% disclose a metric they track over time, so AI has won the capex war but has to win the ROI war. Inside tech, correlations have collapsed to unusually low levels. TMT is September's most net-bought US sector and Mag 7 inflows sit at a three-year 95th percentile, but the money is rotating: software is the most net-bought Info Tech subsector, semis the most net-sold, and semiconductor earnings revisions are rolling over. The Nasdaq is consolidating in a tight range. Per Bloomberg's Crook, it looks poised for a move, direction unclear.
